trap_description: Over-engineering simple requirements into complex generic monads, ABCs, or type acrobatics
bad_example: Creating AbstractGenericHandlerFactory<TReq, TRes> for a single 5-line string transform
remediation_rule: Start with pure functions or simple structs; introduce interfaces only when multiple concrete implementations exist.

trap_description: Catching broad exceptions and returning None or empty lists without logging or caller notification
bad_example: try: do_work() except Exception: return None
remediation_rule: Catch specific exceptions only; preserve error stack traces or return explicit Result.err(e).

trap_description: Generating Java-style Class hierarchies with private properties and redundant getters/setters
bad_example: class User { private name: string; public getName() { return this.name; } }
remediation_rule: Use plain readonly TypeScript interfaces and immutable data objects: export interface User { readonly name: string; }

trap_description: Using mutable objects (list, dict) as default parameter values in function definitions
remediation_rule: Always use None as default: def append_item(item, target: list | None = None): if target is None: target = []

trap_description: Passing untyped dictionary or loose tuple payloads across module boundaries without validation
remediation_rule: Use Pydantic v2 models or Zod schemas at external and boundary interfaces to guarantee shape.

trap_description: Returning naked errors from internal calls without context wrapping or sentinel checks
remediation_rule: Wrap with descriptive context: return fmt.Errorf(\failed to load user %s: %w\"

trap_description: Reaching for Go channels and goroutines for basic synchronized state protection
bad_example: Creating a background actor goroutine with 3 channels just to protect an int counter
remediation_rule: Use sync.Mutex or sync/atomic for shared in-memory state; reserve channels for signaling and data streams.

trap_description: Exporting single-implementation interfaces from the provider package before any consumer needs it
bad_example: package userdb; type Service interface { GetUser() }; type service struct {}
remediation_rule: Define interfaces at the consumer package where dependencies are injected, not in the provider package.

trap_description: Liberally calling .clone() across structs to bypass borrow checker errors without understanding ownership
remediation_rule: Borrow with & / &mut; redesign struct ownership, use Arc for shared immutable state, or use ID handles.

trap_description: Using 'as any' or loose type casting to bypass complex compiler errors
remediation_rule: Use type guards, discriminated unions, or z.infer<typeof Schema> to safely narrow types.

trap_description: Bare 'except:' or 'except Exception:' catching system exit, keyboard interrupt, or masked bugs
remediation_rule: Catch specific expected exceptions (e.g. (KeyError, ValueError)), log with exc_info, or let it propagate.
